name: bm-r6-perlecan-growth-perturbations
title: Perlecan & growth perturbations on cell shape
claim: Carrying an inferred collagen lifetime through BM relaxation to cell shape reproduces the paper's intervention ordering: perlecan gain gives taller cells than control, and loss gives flatter ones, with the inferred relaxation time (turnover) kept distinct from the predicted cell height (mechanics).
experiment: Run the TurnoverShapeProcess pipeline for four conditions -- control, perlecan gain, perlecan loss, and fast growth. The inferred collagen IV lifetime (modulated by a perlecan factor) sets the BM relaxation time (inferred_relaxation = collagen_lifetime x perlecan_factor); that relaxation drives the reduced-order prism mechanics (R1) to a predicted cell height. Read inferred_relaxation (the turnover/inference quantity) and cell_height / confinement (the independent mechanical prediction) at the end of each 40-step run (dt 0.2), and check the rank-order against Barrientos Figure 7.
result: The intervention ordering reproduces exactly. Predicted cell height is tallest under perlecan gain (0.4386), then control (0.4287), then perlecan loss (0.4043) -- a strict gain > control > loss ordering, matching Figure 7. The inferred relaxation time scales exactly linearly with the perlecan factor (inferred_relaxation = 5.0 x perlecan_factor: 1.5 at loss, 5.0 at control, 10.0 at gain, 15.0 at a factor of 3), and is reported as a separate output from the predicted height, so the inferred (turnover) and predicted (mechanics) quantities stay distinct as the plan requires. The fast-growth condition (shorter doubling time) collapses the cell to height 0.134 -- faster proliferation spreads the cell far more strongly than perlecan changes it. The perlecan-driven height differences are small in magnitude (~2-3% gain-vs-control at these parameters) while strictly ordered; the growth-rate axis dominates cell shape.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition: A reproduced intervention ordering (perlecan gain > control > loss) with the inferred relaxation kept distinct from the predicted shape closes the P1-era reproduction and feeds the predictive-feedback study (E4).

question: Does the inferred chain lifetime -> relaxation -> shape reproduce the paper's perlecan and growth-rate intervention ordering?

purpose.question: Does the inferred chain (collagen lifetime -> BM relaxation -> cell shape) reproduce the paper's perlecan and growth-rate intervention ordering, keeping inferred and predicted quantities distinct?
purpose.mechanism: Perlecan stabilizes collagen IV, lengthening its inferred molecular lifetime; a longer lifetime is a slower BM relaxation time, which the reduced-order prism mechanics (R1) turns into a taller (more confined) cell. The turnover-inferred relaxation and the mechanics-predicted shape are two distinct outputs of the pipeline.
purpose.expected_outcome: A strict cell-height ordering perlecan gain > control > loss (Fig 7), with inferred_relaxation scaling with the perlecan factor and reported separately from the predicted height.

hypothesis: Propagating inferred collagen lifetime distributions for control, perlecan gain/loss and growth-rate changes through the relaxation->shape chain reproduces the relative cell- morphology ordering and uncertainty of Figure 7, keeping inferred and independently predicted outcomes distinct.
objective: Use inferred collagen lifetime distributions for control, perlecan gain/loss and growth-rate conditions; propagate parameter uncertainty through relaxation and shape; compare relative cell morphology and uncertainty to Fig 7 while keeping inferred vs predicted outcomes distinct.
description:
Closes the reproduction campaign by propagating the turnover-inference results (Fig 3-6)
into predicted shapes (Fig 7). Collagen lifetime distributions for control, perlecan
gain/loss and growth-rate perturbations drive the relaxation->shape chain with explicit
uncertainty propagation. The study must keep quantities that are INFERRED from the timer
observation model distinct from quantities INDEPENDENTLY PREDICTED by the mechanical model,
per the plan's validation distinction.
key_assumptions: Perlecan modulates the collagen IV lifetime multiplicatively (perlecan_factor); >1 stabilizes (longer lifetime), <1 destabilizes.
The inferred collagen lifetime, times the perlecan factor, IS the BM relaxation time (turnover -> relaxation).
The predicted cell shape is the R1 reduced-order prism mechanics run with that relaxation (perlecan does not act on the mechanics except through the relaxation time).
inferred_relaxation (turnover/inference) and cell_height (mechanics prediction) are kept as distinct outputs; the inferred quantity is not re-derived from the predicted one.

Reduced units; relative morphology ordering is the claim, not absolute cell height. Uncertainty bands over the inferred lifetime distribution are a documented follow-up (point estimates recorded here).

baseline.name: bm-r6-perlecan-growth-perturbations
baseline.note: The chain from turnover to shape. An inferred collagen IV lifetime, adjusted for perlecan, sets the basement-membrane relaxation time, which the homogeneous tissue model turns into a predicted cell shape. Perlecan that stabilizes collagen lengthens the lifetime and confines the cells, so the model reproduces the paper's ordering of the perlecan and growth-rate interventions: perlecan gain gives the tallest cells, then the control, then perlecan loss. Quantities inferred from the turnover data are kept separate from the shapes the mechanics predicts.

falsifiability: The claim would be overturned if the predicted cell-height ordering were not strictly perlecan gain > control > loss (an inverted or collapsed ordering), if inferred_relaxation did not increase with the perlecan factor, if the pipeline failed to emit the inferred relaxation and the predicted height as distinct outputs, or if a faster growth rate did not spread the cell. Any of these would show the turnover->shape chain does not reproduce the Fig 7 intervention ordering or violate the inferred-vs-predicted distinction. The deterministic contracts in tests/test_turnover_shape.py would fail in that case.

limitations: Reduced units; the claim is the RELATIVE morphology ordering, not absolute cell height.

Perlecan-driven height differences are small in magnitude (~2-3% gain vs control at these parameters); the ordering is strict but the sensitivity is modest, while the growth-rate axis dominates shape.

Point estimates only: the Fig 7 result propagates an inferred-lifetime DISTRIBUTION with uncertainty bands; this study records the point-estimate ordering and leaves the uncertainty propagation as a documented follow-up.
The inferred collagen lifetime is an input parameter here, not re-inferred from a turnover observation model (Fig 3-6); the inference step is upstream (R3-era) and assumed.
Homogeneous single cell via the R1 endpoint; no spatial epithelium.

config.title: Intervention ordering on cell height (Fig 7 reproduction)
config.caption: Predicted cell height for each perlecan and growth-rate condition, with the inferred membrane relaxation time marked on each bar, reproducing the paper's Figure 7. Perlecan gain gives the tallest cells, then the control, then perlecan loss.

report.title: R6 -- turnover -> shape intervention ordering (Fig 7 reproduction)
report.verdict: The turnover -> relaxation -> shape pipeline reproduces Barrientos Figure 7's intervention ordering on a deterministic run: predicted cell height is tallest under perlecan gain (0.439), then control (0.429), then perlecan loss (0.404), and the inferred BM relaxation time scales exactly with the perlecan factor (5.0 x factor) while being reported as a distinct output from the predicted shape. The fast-growth condition collapses the cell to 0.134, showing the growth-rate axis dominates morphology. The perlecan effect is strictly ordered but small in magnitude; uncertainty-band propagation over the inferred-lifetime distribution is a documented follow-up.
report.main_insight: Carrying an inferred collagen lifetime (x perlecan) through the BM relaxation time into the R1 mechanics reproduces the paper's perlecan intervention ordering and keeps the inferred (turnover) and predicted (mechanics) quantities distinct, as the validation plan requires.
report.caveat: Reduced units and point estimates only; the perlecan-driven height differences are modest (~2-3%), and the growth-rate axis dominates shape -- the strength of the result is the robust ordering and the inferred/predicted separation, not the magnitude of the perlecan effect.

findings.statement: The pipeline reproduces Figure 7's intervention ordering: predicted cell height is tallest under perlecan gain (0.4386), then control (0.4287), then perlecan loss (0.4043) -- a strict gain > control > loss ordering.
findings.explanation: Perlecan gain lengthens the inferred collagen lifetime, slowing BM relaxation, so the R1 mechanics keep the cell taller; perlecan loss does the reverse.
findings.next_action: feed the closed reproduction campaign into the E4 predictive-feedback study

findings.statement: The inferred BM relaxation time (turnover) and the predicted cell height (mechanics) are distinct pipeline outputs; the inferred relaxation scales exactly linearly with the perlecan factor (5.0 x factor: 1.5 / 5.0 / 10.0 / 15.0), and perlecan reaches the predicted shape only through that relaxation time.

evidence.observed: inferred_relaxation = 5.0 x perlecan_factor, exact; emitted separately from cell_height

findings.explanation: The pipeline reports inferred_relaxation and cell_height as separate outputs, satisfying the plan's inferred-vs-predicted validation distinction.

findings.statement: The growth-rate axis dominates cell shape (fast growth collapses height to 0.134 vs control 0.429), while the perlecan-driven height differences are small in magnitude (~2-3% gain vs control). The Fig 7 ordering is robust, but the model's perlecan sensitivity is modest.
findings.next_action: propagate the inferred-lifetime uncertainty bands to test whether the perlecan ordering survives the distribution width

followup_proposals.title: Propagate the inferred-lifetime uncertainty bands through to the predicted shape
followup_proposals.motivation: Figure 7 carries uncertainty bands from the inferred collagen-lifetime distribution. This study records point-estimate ordering; propagate the distribution (sample the inferred lifetime per condition) and test whether the perlecan ordering survives the band width given the modest ~2-3% effect.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: The perlecan ordering may overlap within the inferred-lifetime uncertainty, which would weaken the reproduction from strict to distributional.

resolved_uncertainties: The turnover->shape pipeline reproduces the Fig 7 perlecan intervention ordering.
Inferred (turnover) and predicted (mechanics) quantities are kept distinct, as the plan requires.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether the perlecan ordering survives uncertainty-band propagation given the modest ~2-3% effect.
Absolute cell shape in physical units.

biological_validation.basis: Reproduces Fig 7's intervention ordering (perlecan gain > control > loss) with the inferred relaxation kept distinct from the predicted shape. Magnitude of the perlecan effect is modest (noted as a limitation), but the ordering and the inferred/predicted split are robust.

explanatory_gain.basis: Shows the growth-rate axis dominates cell shape over the perlecan axis, and provides the closed turnover->shape chain the predictive-feedback study (E4) builds on.

expert_questions: Magnitude: the perlecan-driven height difference is only ~2-3% at these parameters. Is the strict ordering a sufficient reproduction of Fig 7, or should the perlecan sensitivity (how strongly the lifetime maps to relaxation, and relaxation to shape) be recalibrated to match the paper's effect size?

Uncertainty: should the canonical R6 run propagate the inferred collagen-lifetime DISTRIBUTION (uncertainty bands), rather than the point estimates recorded here, before the reproduction is called complete?
